target._notes: Fixed configuration — the cartridge build never changes; firmware must stay <= 23.0.1 (23.5.0 patches the fs Path::Normalize bug). The engine validates modules.*.first_page_sha256 before trusting any other value in this file.

main._notes: base = main_base from the dumper log / dump header (core.js: main_base = exe_addr - 0x1AF7FA0). size = sum of the contiguous main_* regions from dumper phase B (dump_recv.py manifest.json). first_page_sha256 = sha256 of the first 0x1000 bytes of the main region file, computed offline.

sdk._notes: base = sdk_base (core.js: sdk_base = memcpy_addr - 0x5224E0). size = sum of sdk_* regions from phase B, or SCAN_LIMIT if phase B failed. first_page_sha256 computed from the sdk region file's first 0x1000 bytes.

svc._notes_all: Values are sdk-relative offsets of the wrapper ENTRY (the `movz x8,#imm` instruction), not the svc instruction — call_rop controls x0-x5 only, x8 must be loaded by the wrapper itself. Filled by dumper phase A (in-process) and cross-checked offline with: python3 tools/svc_scan.py dumps/<run>/sdk_<base>.bin --base 0x<base> --out svc.json. Ground-truth svc numbers: repos/ns2jb/engine/switch2/ro/payload/start.S (see offsets/README.md).

_notes.query_memory: svc 0x06 — dumper phase A entry + phase B arg-mode detection (3-arg canonical vs 2-arg `mov x2,x1`).
_notes.cancel_synchronization: svc 0x19 on Switch 2 — CORRECTION of the earlier 0x53 guess (the Switch 1 number): the ns2jb hardware-proven cancel wrapper pin '210300d4c0035fd6' (SmileBASIC sdk+0x158414) executes `svc #0x19; ret`, and start.S-era numbering confirms Switch 2 reshuffled the table. Confirm on the Civ 7 sdk dump via svc_scan.py svc_all (search `svc #0x19`) or Ghidra.
_notes.get_system_tick: svc 0x1E — dumper phase A / svc_scan (start.S uses the svc, not mrs cntvct_el0).

sdk_offsets._notes_all: sdk-relative offsets. memcpy/longjmp/pthread_* first located by tools/svc_scan.py candidates (setjmp/longjmp/pthread-family heuristics), then CONFIRMED by manual RE in Ghidra (load the sdk region file at its base). setjmp is not in the DESIGN schema but record it in jmp_buf work anyway. The event_*/affinity/sha256 entries below feed the app modules ported off the SmileBASIC pin tables (app/events.cjs, app/affinity.cjs, app/filesystem.cjs nativeHash, ro/worker-control.cjs) — every one fails loudly naming its key until filled.

_notes.longjmp: svc_scan longjmp candidates (ldp x19..x30,[x0] run + mov sp restore) — confirm in Ghidra; determine jmp_buf format.
_notes.pthread_create: svc_scan pthread_create candidates (callers of a CreateThread svc region) — confirm in Ghidra.
_notes.pthread_join: svc_scan pthread_join candidates (callers of a WaitSynchronization+CloseHandle region) — confirm in Ghidra.
_notes.pthread_exit: svc_scan pthread_exit candidates (terminal svc sites / tail-callers) — confirm in Ghidra.
_notes.memset: manual Ghidra RE (callee of the calloc/memcpy neighborhood); cross-check the byte-fill loop shape.
_notes.memcpy: ALREADY KNOWN from core.js:776 — sdk_base = *(main+0x4DC6088) - 0x5224E0, i.e. memcpy offset 0x5224E0 (5389792). Verify against the dump in Ghidra.
_notes.set_affinity: pthread_setaffinity_np (app/affinity.cjs pin): manual Ghidra RE — search for callers of a SetThreadCoreMask svc region (Switch 2 number via svc_scan). SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1261024.
_notes.event_initialize: nn::os::InitializeEvent(EventType*, bool initial, EventClearMode) — wave start-gate constructor (app/events.cjs). Ghidra: the caller pair of svc WaitForAddress(0x34-style)/SignalToAddress storing the {state byte, clear-mode byte} two-byte header. SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1198256.
_notes.event_signal: nn::os::SignalEvent(EventType*) — releases wave gates / notifier workers (app/events.cjs). SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1198320.
_notes.event_clear: nn::os::ClearEvent(EventType*) — gate reset before wave retries (app/events.cjs). SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1198608.
_notes.event_finalize: nn::os::FinalizeEvent(EventType*) — gate teardown after joins (app/events.cjs). SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1198304.
_notes.event_wait: nn::os::WaitEvent(EventType*) — the workers' first native call (start gate; the state-spin + WaitForAddress loop). SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1198656.
_notes.get_affinity: pthread_getaffinity_np (app/affinity.cjs read-back verification). SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1260864.
_notes.available_core_mask: nn::os::GetThreadAvailableCoreMask() — the allowed set wave core pinning validates against (app/affinity.cjs). Ghidra: adrp/ldr/br thunk into the os ThreadManager, or a GetInfo-based implementation. SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1218016.
_notes.current_core_number: nn::os::GetCurrentCoreNumber() — qualification worker identity check (app/affinity.cjs currentCoreCall). SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1217872.
_notes.sha256: OPTIONAL — on-console one-shot SHA-256 (SmileBASIC reference: nnSdk GenerateSha256Hash at sdk+19648, x0=out,x1=32,x2=data,x3=len). While null, app/filesystem.cjs nativeHash verifies via full read-back + host-side hash (weaker single-source check, recorded per call); fill it to restore the console-computed hash path.

timing._notes_all: Counter-frequency ground truth for app/timing.cjs (wave receive-order timing). Upstream story: the SmileBASIC SDK wrapper returned a hardcoded 19.2 MHz (the Switch 1 value), so ns2jb probed a SECOND module — nnCompatThin, uniquely identified by its r-x mapping size 45989888 — whose getter at +0x13d6f0 returned the true 31.25 MHz. For Civ 7, M0 RE must answer: which module reports the truthful frequency, what uniquely identifies its mapping, and where the getter lives. The engine keeps the runtime probe: unique-mapping check, executable check, optional instruction pin, and the returned value must equal expected_frequency.

_notes.frequency_module_size: r-x mapping size that UNIQUELY identifies the module holding the true frequency getter (SmileBASIC reference: 45989888 = nnCompatThin). Measure from the dumper phase-B map / memory-map.json.
_notes.frequency_offset: offset within that module of the frequency getter (SmileBASIC reference: 0x13d6f0, a movz/movk constant builder returning 31250000).
_notes.frequency_bytes: OPTIONAL hex pin of the getter's opening instructions (SmileBASIC reference: '00ca9a52803ba072c0035fd6', 12 bytes). Until filled, verify() checks executability and warns.
_notes.expected_frequency: the true Switch 2 counter frequency in Hz — 31250000, hardware-verified by the ns2jb run; verify() fails if the getter returns anything else.
_notes.sdk_frequency: OPTIONAL sdk-relative offset of the SDK's own GetTickFrequency equivalent (SmileBASIC reference: sdk+1218160, returned the lying 19200000). Recorded for comparison only.
_notes.sdk_expected_frequency: OPTIONAL — when non-null (with sdk_frequency), the SDK wrapper's return is cross-checked against it. Civ 7's value is an M0 RE question: its nnSdk may already be truthful.

mounts._notes_all: nnSdk mount-table walk (app/inspect-mounts.cjs walker + app/mounted-save.cjs borrow; consumed by the donor FS in ro/files.cjs and the wave scratch mounts in memory/probe-reserved-gap.cjs). Every value is null until M0 RE maps Civ 7's nn::fs mount structures — the reference values below are the SmileBASIC capture (run3 nnSdk) that the upstream walker hardware-proved; Civ 7's nnSdk is a different build, so re-derive each one in Ghidra from the dump (find the mount-name strings 'save'/'rom' in the sdk and walk back to the table). The SmileBASIC verifiedFunctions instruction pins are replaced by modules.*.first_page_sha256 + pins.region_hashes.

_notes.table_offset: sdk-relative address of the intrusive-list head of mounted filesystems (SmileBASIC reference: 13748384 = 0xD1C8A0).
_notes.head_first: offset within the head structure of the pointer to the first mount's link block; the walk terminates when the chain returns to the head address (SmileBASIC reference: 8).
_notes.accessor_backlink: link-block address minus the accessor-object base (SmileBASIC reference: 8).
_notes.accessor_name: offset of the mount-name field within the accessor object (SmileBASIC reference: 24).
_notes.accessor_name_bytes: width of the mount-name field (SmileBASIC reference: 16; names like save/tmp/rom, NUL-padded).
_notes.accessor_implementation: offset of the implementation pointer within the accessor object (SmileBASIC reference: 40).
_notes.accessor_next: offset of the next-link pointer within the accessor object (= link block + 8; SmileBASIC reference: 16).
_notes.implementation_service: offset of the fsp-srv service pointer within the implementation object (SmileBASIC reference: 16).
_notes.service_vtable: offset of the vtable pointer within the service object (SmileBASIC reference: 0).
_notes.service_manager: offset of the session-manager pointer within the service object (SmileBASIC reference: 16).
_notes.service_object_id: offset of the u32 domain object id within the service object (SmileBASIC reference: 24; also the root object id in cloneMountedRoot).
_notes.manager_magic_offset: u32 offset within the session-manager state checked as a magic (SmileBASIC reference: offset 8, value 2048 = 0x800).
_notes.manager_magic_value: the expected magic value at manager_magic_offset (SmileBASIC reference: 2048).
_notes.manager_state_offset: second checked u32 within the manager state (SmileBASIC reference: offset 92 = 0x5c).
_notes.manager_slots: offset of the session-slots pointer within the manager state; the first slot's u32 is the borrowed session handle (SmileBASIC reference: 16).
_notes.proxy_global: sdk-relative address of the nn::fs filesystem-proxy service global used to clone the SDK filesystem domain (SmileBASIC reference: 13748448 = 0xD1C900, 64 bytes past the mount table).
_notes.proxy_init_flag_offset: byte offset within that global of the initialized flag (bit 0 set when the proxy holds a live service; SmileBASIC reference: 8).
_notes.names: mount names the walker captures deeply (service/vtable bytes) and mounted-save.cjs will borrow, e.g. ["save","tmp"] — expected for Civ 7: save (donor + canary) and, if the game holds it, tmp (wave scratch); Civ 7 also holds rom (the mounted-rom path uses its own walker). If tmp is absent, the tmp-based flows need a different secondary mount — record what the game actually holds.

jmp_buf._notes: Derived by manual RE in Ghidra from the confirmed longjmp/setjmp pair: register order in the save run (svc_scan prints the stp offsets), whether pc/sp are pointer-mangled (svc_scan mangled_hint: nearby mrs tpidr_el0 / autiasp), and if mangled, the TLS guard slot offset.

gadgets._notes_all: main-module absolute runtime vaddrs (main_base + offset from gadget_scan on the main region file). Fill per M2 wave-chain needs; gadget_scan --find <name> --base 0x<main_base>. BarbarismJB engine note: the five ropchain-builder entries (args_loader, frame_ldp, indirect_call, load_x21, store_result) must be MAIN-MODULE-RELATIVE offsets, not absolute vaddrs — engine/shared/frames.cjs buildRopChain resolves them against the live main base from the CIV1 hello.

_notes.exit_thread: gadget_scan --find b_to --arg <pthread_exit vaddr> after pthread_exit is confirmed.
_notes.blr_after_ldp: gadget_scan --find blr_after_ldp (per-chain; add more entries as the M2 chains are built).
_notes.args_loader: ropchain builder entry (main-relative): 'ldp x2,x3,[sp,#0x10]; ldp x0,x1,[sp],#0x20; ldp x4,x5,[sp],#0x10; mov sp,x29; ldp x29,x30,[sp],#0x10; ret'. Pre-pinned from CivSwitch core.js gadget10 (main+0x2e09e3c) for this build; re-verify in the dump.
_notes.frame_ldp: ropchain builder entry (main-relative): 'ldp x20,x19,[sp,#0x10]; ldp x29,x30,[sp],#0x20; ret'. core.js gadget11 (main+0x1c4).
_notes.indirect_call: ropchain builder entry (main-relative): 'ldr x8,[x20]; ldp x20,x19,[sp,#0x20]; ldp x22,x21,[sp,#0x10]; ldr x6,[x8,#0x18]; ldp x29,x30,[sp],#0x30; br x6'. core.js gadget12 (main+0xca74c8) — the call gadget: target loaded via a host-built pointer chain.
_notes.load_x21: ropchain builder entry (main-relative): 'ldr x21,[sp,#0x10]; ldp x29,x30,[sp],#0x30; ret'. core.js gadget13 (main+0x39b4).
_notes.store_result: ropchain builder entry (main-relative): 'str x0,[x21]; ldp x30,x21,[sp],#0x20; ret'. core.js gadget14 (main+0x2c97530) — saves each native call's x0 into the worker result area.

pins._notes: sha256 of each dumped region file, copied from dump_recv.py's manifest.json. The engine compares these before using anything in this file on a new session.
